scope: Real historical interpreters compiled and executed on the current Linux host; not every minor release, OS version, terminal or distro.

source_builds.name: Bash 1.14.7
source_builds.extraction: Regular files and directories only; archived symlinks omitted.

source_patches.diff:
--- a/config.h
+++ b/config.h
@@ -63,7 +63,7 @@
 /* Define READLINE to get the nifty/glitzy editing features.
    This is on by default.  You can turn it off interactively
    with the -nolineediting flag. */
-#define READLINE
+/* READLINE disabled for compatibility test build */
 
 /* Define BANG_HISTORY if you want to have Csh style "!" history expansion.
    This is unrelated to READLINE. */

--- a/machines.h
+++ b/machines.h
@@ -889,8 +889,9 @@
 #    define HAVE_STRERROR
 #    define VOID_SIGHANDLER
 #    define HAVE_SYS_SIGLIST
-#    define HAVE_VFPRINTF
-#    define HAVE_VARARGS_H
+#    undef HAVE_VFPRINTF
+#    define HAVE_STDARG_H
+#    define HAVE_WAIT_H
 #    define SEARCH_LIB_NEEDS_SPACE
 #    if defined (__GNUC__)
 #      define HAVE_FIXED_INCLUDES

--- a/siglist.h
+++ b/siglist.h
@@ -33,7 +33,7 @@
 extern char *sys_siglist[];
 #endif /* !Solaris && !Linux && !__BSD_4_4__ && !Minix && !NetBSD && !FreeBSD && !BSD_OS */
 
-#if !defined (strsignal) && !defined (Solaris) && !defined (NetBSD)
+#if !defined (strsignal) && !defined (Solaris) && !defined (NetBSD) && !defined (Linux)
 #  define strsignal(sig) (char *)sys_siglist[sig]
 #endif /* !strsignal && !Solaris && !NetBSD */

--- a/unwind_prot.h
+++ b/unwind_prot.h
@@ -35,7 +35,7 @@
 
 /* How to protect a pointer to a string. */
 #define unwind_protect_string(X) \
-  unwind_protect_var ((int *)&(X), (X), sizeof (char *))
+  unwind_protect_var ((int *)&(X), (char *)&(X), sizeof (char *))
 
 /* How to protect any old pointer. */
 #define unwind_protect_pointer(X) unwind_protect_string (X)

patch_rationale: Select the historical Linux platform rules on x86_64; this does not force a 32-bit ABI.
Disable obsolete varargs/vfprintf and readline paths; use libc sys/wait.h and strsignal.
Adapt unwind_protect_string to copy a 64-bit pointer value correctly.
This is a patched old interpreter on a modern host, not an unmodified historical OS image.

patch_rationale: Rename getline to avoid the libc name collision.
Avoid duplicate RLIMIT_OFILE/NOFILE switch cases on Linux.
Use modern no-argument getpgrp, thread-local errno and strerror.
Generate Linux signal names/descriptions from the host Python signal module.
This test build does not certify the complete historical interpreter or OS.

collector_limits.gnu_timeout: 350 ms per helper, then 100 ms kill grace.
collector_limits.posix_watchdog: TERM after one second, KILL one second later; direct child only.
collector_limits.capture_limit: ulimit -f 512 shell file-size blocks; normally 256 or 512 KiB depending on shell.
collector_limits.process_scan: At most min(configured process_limit, 512) proc entries; the rank is over readable sampled entries.
collector_limits.wall_clock: No overall hard wall-clock worker deadline in the portable backend. Per-helper limits, output caps and scan counts do not prevent uninterruptible kernel/filesystem waits.
collector_limits.io_semantics: Linux read_bytes + write_bytes are cumulative bytes, not rates; other Unix per-process I/O remains unavailable.
collector_limits.memory_semantics: Darwin/BSD free pages are labeled free, never Linux MemAvailable.
collector_limits.service_semantics: launchd shows visible bootstrap jobs; BSD service -e lists enabled scripts and does not prove running state.
collector_limits.charset: Portable text is normalized to printable ASCII for byte-oriented old shells; --unicode uses known single-cell border glyphs.
collector_limits.legacy_dependency: Bash 1.14.7 has no printf builtin; a working external printf is needed.

summary.notes: The 7 fixture tests include real PTY geometry, missing-timeout deadline, unavailable observations and Darwin/BSD parser fixtures. The 18 startup scenarios ran under Bash 1, Bash 2 and Zsh 2 with real interactive PTYs.

integration_comparison_note: Full generated artifact bytes match every tested target after the root embedded the canonical templates. The configurator continues to receive UI-only edits; interpreter evidence is pinned by generated artifact and template hashes.
